correctness.rationale: The expansion is over square-free shift subsets in characteristic at least five, and subtraction at the four omitted starts costs at most 32. Distinct pairs have sum -1 (away from one root the ratio of the two linear factors is a bijection onto the field minus 1); the singleton sums vanish. The four smooth cubics have one rational point at infinity and the monic quartic has two, giving Hasse contributions 8 sqrt(q) and 2 sqrt(q)+1 respectively. Thus 16 N_q >= q-10 sqrt(q)-39 is strictly positive above 169. I reproduced the entire finite census, including every missing mask, by passing to norms to the prime field: the quadratic character of a nonzero element is the Legendre symbol of its norm. Quadratic norms use a^2-d b^2; the cubic at 125 uses the multiplication determinant in a different irreducible basis X^3+2X+1. This checks 42 fields, the first success at 37 and the last failure at 53, with 59 the next eligible order. In characteristic three shifts zero and three coincide; characteristic two separately allows no nonsquare.
residual_risks: 59 is the first eligible field order in the universal tail, not the smallest arbitrary integer lower bound (there is no eligible order strictly between 53 and 59). The theoretical tail is not inferred from the census.

originality.rationale: The prime-field part evaluates an already supplied exact all-word formula, whose trace and constant tables plus Hasse give the same finite reduction. The extension-field part is a direct consequence of a distinct indexed five-word theorem and its complete exception table, by projecting to either end and including the sole possible orphan start in characteristic five. This covers the exact nonprime exception list and even the missing masks. The dates of the two indexed records do not establish priority; this is a judgment of mathematical coverage.
residual_risks: The same-date extension-field records were not placed in priority order. The exact consequence is established irrespective of priority.

value.rationale: A sharp field-size cutoff and the anomalous extension orders are natural questions. Here the best candidate remainder, the exact extension exceptions 25 and 49, is already obtained from the complete five-word table by projecting and including one missing start. The prime remainder is evaluation of known exact counts in a routine Hasse-bounded range. Independent arithmetic corroboration does not supply a distinct new exact invariant, and there is no valuable surviving claim to repair.
residual_risks: The primes cutoff is not printed verbatim in the inspected count theorem; the assessment is of what is already determined, not its wording.
